engagement_title: Ironline Forge trade fair and brand story: a committed single-tone editorial set off two afternoons on the shop floor, the struck maker's mark recovered off a sand-cast bracket, twelve casting spec cards merged from last year's printed card, and the stand panels handed back editable
vertical: Industrial and manufacturing: a heritage iron and bronze foundry casting bespoke architectural work, selling to specifiers, architects and developers who have never been inside a foundry
real_brief_anchor: Ledger anchor for PHOTO-23, carrying both grounding notes the ledger holds. Upwork, quoted as far as the ledger carries it: 'Adapted from a real Upwork logo + challenge-coin vectorization brief (cand_38, db_i 95): the client already HAS hand-mocked concept art and needs it turned into polished, true vector artwork for a primary crest plus several symbolic coin-face designs, coin-ready and readable at small sizes, with versions that reproduce in flat black, reversed white, and struck gold and silver metal, deliverable as clean scalable vector plus product-ready exports for a mint/manufacturer handoff.' Freelancer.com, quoted as far as the ledger carries it: 'Adapted from a real Freelancer.com logo brief (the original asked for a mark in fully editable vector format (.ai or .eps), instantly readable at small sizes on labels and swing tags, print-ready CMYK output and scalable vector artwork, shipped with one-colour and reverse variants). Designing a NEW mark from scratch is out of Adobe-connector scope, so the doable, in-scope reading of that same requirement, take what the client actually has and turn it into clean, scalable, production-ready vector artwork plus the one-colour + reverse varia'. Absorbs AO-38 and AO-93. The verdict is REBUILD because the banked concept sat on the imaging surface alone and ended in a tinted set plus a traced mark, which is two deliverables. The fuller commission a foundry in this position genuinely buys, and the shape these are posted in, is the one built here: the mark recovered from the only artefact that carries it and proved at the sizes it will actually reproduce at, the editorial set committed to one tone, the stand panel and story page handed back editable because the next fair is in autumn, and the twelve casting spec cards reprinted off last year's press file. The foundry is the fictional Ironline Forge; no real firm, person, product or trademark is referenced.
client_one_liner: Our mark was cut into a die by somebody's grandfather and exists nowhere as artwork, our photographs were shot half by furnace light and half by roof light, and in March we take a stand in front of architects who have never been inside a foundry.
client_brief:
We have been casting iron and bronze in the same building since 1911, and almost everything we sell now goes to architects and developers who have never set foot in a foundry. In March we take a stand at a trade fair, and we are rebuilding the brand story page at the same time. Both need to look like us and neither does.

What I want is dark, single tone, heavy. The pictures should feel the way the shop floor feels: hot, dirty and precise. Not a clean corporate photo library. We sell permanence at five to sixty thousand a piece and the pictures have to carry that.

The photographs come from two afternoons on the floor. Some are lit by the furnace and some by the roof lights, so I expect they need work.

Then the mark. Every piece we make gets our maker's mark struck into it before it cools. It is on the bracket in the photograph. There is no artwork for it anywhere, there never was, it was cut into a die by somebody's grandfather. I want it back as artwork we can actually use, because it belongs on the panels, on the story page and on the spec cards, and it has to work small and reversed out of the dark.

For the stand I need a tall panel and the story page, and a squarer social version, and I would like those in one file we can change ourselves before the next fair in the autumn.

The spec cards are the leave-behind. Twelve castings, one card each, with the reference, the alloy, the finish, the weight and the lead time. I have last year's print file and the spreadsheet.

If the panel needs a wider shot of a finished installation, we do not have one. Buy it and bill me.

What I need back: the finished pictures, the mark as artwork with a note on where it holds, the panel and story file, the twelve cards ready for the printer, a board, and a note on what you did.
price_band_and_audience: Heritage foundry selling bespoke architectural iron and bronze at five thousand to sixty thousand dollars a piece, to specifiers, architects and developers aged roughly 40 to 65 who are buying craft, permanence and the confidence that the piece will still be there in eighty years. The band is load-bearing throughout. At this level a committed dark single-tone editorial treatment is right because it sells process and provenance rather than product features: the buyer wants to believe there are people and heat behind the piece. Run the same job for a commodity fastener supplier and every choice inverts: that catalogue needs bright, literal, evenly lit product shots on white, and this treatment would read as pretension and misprice the offer badly. The band also governs the mark. A maker's mark struck into iron is proof of origin at this price, so it has to be recovered faithfully rather than tidied into a fashionable monoline, and it has to hold at the smallest place it appears, because a specifier reading a spec card is exactly the person the mark is meant to reassure. The collateral follows: generous type, plenty of black, numbers set plainly and honestly, nothing that reads as promotional. Bright, energetic, offer-shaped design here would tell an architect this is a supplier rather than a workshop. The ledger records the base concept at 900 to 1,800 dollars; this full trade-fair commission, with the mark recovery, the editable panels and the twelve-record card run, sits at 2,200 to 4,000 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.sector: A heritage iron and bronze foundry casting bespoke architectural work for specifiers and developers.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Casting since 1911 in the same Sheffield works; a small crew of founders, patternmakers and finishers.
brand_identity.about: Ironline Forge casts bespoke iron and bronze for architects and developers who have mostly never stood on a foundry floor. We sell permanence and provenance: the heat, the hands, and the fact that the piece will still be here in eighty years. The brand has to feel like the shop floor, hot, dirty and precise.
brand_identity.audience: Specifiers, architects and developers, 40 to 65, buying craft and confidence rather than a catalogue product.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Bespoke castings from five to sixty thousand dollars a piece, priced on provenance and never presented as a promotion.
brand_identity.typography: A generous editorial serif for headlines with plenty of black around it, and a strong grotesque for labels and spec lines. Numbers are set plainly.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, declarative, unshowy. Example line: 'Iron and bronze, cast in this building since 1911.'
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Our maker's mark was cut into a die generations ago and survives only struck into the metal. There is no artwork for it anywhere, and the trade-fair stand and the brand story page are being rebuilt at the same time.
brand_identity.values: Process and provenance over polish. The struck maker's mark must be recovered faithfully rather than tidied into a fashion monoline, and it has to hold small and reversed out of the dark.

assets_supplied.name: ironline_floor_frames/ (14 frames, 4,000 to 4,600px long edge)
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Two afternoons on the shop floor." The pour, hand-finishing a bronze balustrade section, castings cooling on the sand, the pattern racks, the roller door and the yard.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Five of the fourteen are lit only by the furnace, so their entire tonal range is compressed into a narrow band of orange and, once mapped onto a single tone ramp, the castings stop separating from the sand floor around them. Separately, three of the handheld frames carry a slight roll in the shop-floor line that reads as level in a full frame and becomes obvious the moment a tall panel crop is struck from them.

assets_supplied.name: ironline_maker_mark_casting.jpg
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The bracket with our maker's mark struck into it. That is the only place it exists." A 4,200px frame of a sand-cast iron bracket photographed on the bench, the mark struck into the face inside a raised border ring.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The mark is struck into raw sand-cast iron, so its enclosed counters and the gap inside its border ring carry the same pitted grey as the face around them, with no colour and no medium of its own to name. A trace of it reads convincingly at full canvas and closes its counters solid at the size the mark actually reproduces on a spec card and reversed on the dark ground, and the border ring means a background removal returns a filled disc rather than a mark. There is no option on the tracing step to tune any of this.

assets_supplied.name: ironline_spec_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's spec card, the file the printer used." A real press PDF of a single-sided leave-behind card carrying the casting reference, the name, the alloy and finish line, the weight and lead-time line, and a photograph frame, printed and font-embedded.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The card shows four cleanly separated blocks and a picture, which says nothing about how many frames the conversion will actually produce. Worse, the mapping readout's account of the card's story omits one run entirely (the reference line) while keeping the line break that followed it, so the string still looks well formed and every character offset after that point is short by that run's length, and the validator returns VALID on the wrong offsets with no warnings at all.

assets_supplied.name: ironline_castings.csv
assets_supplied.visible_description: The twelve castings with reference, name, alloy, finish, weight, lead time and an image column naming the frame each card should carry.
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two castings were never photographed on their own, so both rows name the same shop-floor frame, and two of the names run to two lines where last year's card carried one. The weight and lead-time columns are also typed inconsistently across the rows, which is a copy decision the agent has to make rather than anything a tool reports.

assets_supplied.name: ironline_story_copy.txt
assets_supplied.visible_description: The brand story text, the stand panel headline and standfirst, the social caption, the dark ground the story page and panels use, and the delivered size of each placement including the physical dimensions of the stand panel.

acceptance_bar: The editorial set reads as one committed dark treatment across the whole shop floor, with no frame collapsing into a single undifferentiated field and nothing giving away that the frames came from two different light sources.
The maker's mark is placeable, scalable artwork with a real viewBox, no opaque full-canvas ground path behind it, and delivered on-dark and single-colour colourways.

The mark holds at the size it actually reproduces on a spec card and reversed on the dark ground, or the note says plainly that it does not, at what size it stops working, and what carries those placements instead.
The mark is recovered rather than redrawn. It still reads as the mark struck into the bracket, not as a tidied modern version of it.
No invented pixels anywhere. No delivered file exceeds its source dimensions, and the note lists every picture any tool resized, downscaled or extended, and by how much.
Every crop is composed for the placement it serves, and no frame with a rolled floor line ships as a tall panel crop.
The stand panel, the brand story page and the social canvas sit in ONE editable file, each keeping its own canvas size, delivered with the self-contained source it was built from.

The words in that file are live text the client can retype, the mark in it is real vector geometry rather than a picture of a mark, and every photograph is a real photograph rather than an empty frame.
One type system across all three canvases, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the weight actually used.
Twelve spec cards, one record per page, in the sheet's order, each carrying the correct casting's photograph rather than one image repeated.
Every mapped field is genuinely present on every card. No field that was mapped is silently missing, and nothing is cut off at trim.
Anything licensed sits with the foundry's own photography under the same tone rather than reading as a bought picture.
The board carries the finished set with nothing silently dropped.
The note states per frame what was applied, the tint hue, strength and grain, the selection wording used to recover the mark, and any frame that could not be brought into the set.

Brings furnace-lit and roof-lit frames onto one base before any style is committed, carries the set to a single dark tone, composes panel and social crops at the sizes they are used at, and recovers a mark that exists only as a struck impression in pitted iron, including the vector hygiene the tracing step does not do.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (mapping and validation calls), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout (recordRange, additionalImageFiles), document_render_layout

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle what lands where: the frames and the mark on imaging, the panel and pages on HTML authoring, the twelve cards on the merge path.
trajectory.judgement: The obvious reading is a grade plus a trace. The real structure is that the mark has to survive two specific reproduction conditions, and one deliverable is defined by being editable in six months.
trajectory.produces: A plan naming deliverable to surface and the confirmed tier.

trajectory.action: Upload the fourteen floor frames, the bracket photograph, last year's card PDF and the casting sheet, holding a manifest with source dimensions.
trajectory.judgement: Source dimensions are recorded here because every no-invented-pixels claim later is made against them, and because the stand panel's true physical size is the one place the set may genuinely run out of pixels.
trajectory.produces: A manifest with source dimensions and a presigned URL per file.

trajectory.action: Preview all fifteen frames and triage: which light each came from, how much tonal range each actually holds, how level the floor line sits, and which frames could carry a tall panel crop at the panel's real dimensions.
trajectory.judgement: Which frames can carry the panel is a question about pixels and about composition at once, and the answer decides the panel design rather than following it.
trajectory.produces: A per-frame triage note naming panel candidates and problem frames.

trajectory.action: Straighten where the floor line rolls and bring both lighting conditions onto one base: exposure, neutral and shadow depth per frame, one call per frame, recording parameters.
trajectory.judgement: A single tone applied on top of two different bases produces two different results from one setting, and the furnace frames need a fundamentally different correction from the roof-light frames to arrive at the same base.
trajectory.produces: Fifteen corrected frames on one base with a per-frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Masked work where a whole-frame move is wrong: hold the glowing pour and the cold sand floor apart by naming the material rather than the object it belongs to.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the entire gate. Naming the substrate returns the substrate; naming a material's own visual properties returns the material. Molten metal and sand want opposite moves that cannot both be served globally.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a global move would have crushed the sand or blown the pour.

trajectory.action: Commit the treatment: choose the tone hue, its strength and the grain, apply across the editorial set one frame at a time, and record the applied settings.
trajectory.judgement: How dark and how committed is the decision the whole look turns on. At this band it has to read as a workshop rather than as a filter, and a batched call applies one identical parameter set to frames that came from two different afternoons.
trajectory.produces: A single-tone editorial master set with applied settings recorded.

trajectory.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, vector recovery
trajectory.action: Recover the mark: a selection worded at what actually distinguishes a struck impression in pitted iron, inverted for polarity, cropped to the returned bounds, traced, then given a viewBox with the opaque ground path removed, plus a solid variant for reversing.
trajectory.judgement: There is no ink here, so the wording that lifts a printed mark off a substrate has nothing to grip and the selection has to be aimed at what the photograph contains. Polarity decides whether the trace is a mark or a filled box, and background removal is the wrong instrument on a mark inside a border ring.
trajectory.produces: A transparent scalable mark plus a solid variant for the dark ground.

trajectory.action: Place the traced mark at the size it reproduces on a spec card and reversed on the dark ground the panels use, and look at both.
trajectory.judgement: The two placements the client named are the two hardest, and neither can be judged at canvas size. Deciding to look at the mark at its real delivered size is the agent's own move.
trajectory.produces: A verdict on the mark at its two hardest placements.

trajectory.action: Produce the colourways the mark needs, on-dark and single-colour, and rasterise a copy locally for the handover bundle and for any placement that cannot take vector.
trajectory.judgement: Which colourways are genuinely needed follows from where the mark actually holds, so this is downstream of the verdict rather than a fixed list.
trajectory.produces: The mark's delivered colourway set plus a rasterised copy.

trajectory.action: Search Stock with short generic queries for a finished architectural metalwork installation, filter to photography, exclude generative results, license and download at full resolution, bring it under the committed tone and lay it beside the tinted set.
trajectory.judgement: Under a single tone the deciding property is luminance structure and black point rather than colour, and a 240 pixel thumbnail carries evidence about neither. Choosing the frame whose structure can join, rather than the best thumbnail, is the whole decision.
trajectory.produces: One licensed camera-scale installation frame, tinted and judged against the set.

trajectory.action: Compose the crops: the tall panel at the panel's real proportion, the story page hero and the social canvas, each framed for its placement, reading each crop's tradeoff metadata and extending a frame at its edges rather than interpolating where the panel needs more height than a frame holds.
trajectory.judgement: The panel is the one placement where the set can genuinely run out of pixels, and the choice between cropping tighter, extending at the edges and moving the placement to another frame changes the panel design. The tradeoffs array is the only signal that a crop interpolated.
trajectory.produces: Composed crops per placement with a resize and extension record.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per typographic role, read the family style inventories for real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to read as a hundred-year-old workshop. Weight cannot be inferred from a style name, a display cut is reached by its own family slug, and one bad name in the kit call discards the valid ones with it.
trajectory.produces: A one-kit type system with family, foundry or designer and real weight per role.

trajectory.action: Author one self-contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes: the stand panel at true physical dimensions, the brand story page and the social canvas. Embed every photograph as image data, place the mark as inline vector inside an explicitly sized and top-left anchored wrapper, and declare family and weight on every text element.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph on this importer, an auto-sized right-anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, weight is not inherited from markup semantics, and a global canvas override collapses a mixed-size set. The design work is how much black the panel carries and how quietly the mark sits at this band.
trajectory.produces: One export-ready HTML carrying all three canvases, uploaded and addressable, retained as a deliverable in its own right.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through both channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at the first canvas, and parse the returned per-canvas markup for the other two, asserting per canvas that every photograph resolved to real image data, that the mark arrived as vector shapes, that the type resolved to the licensed faces, and that nothing sits beyond its declared canvas width.
trajectory.judgement: Treating a successful export as unverified. Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition only ever shows the first canvas.
trajectory.produces: A native editable document with three canvases, an inspected first canvas and a markup audit of the other two.

trajectory.action: Convert last year's spec card PDF to a live document, export IDML, and reconstruct the card's true story text from the document itself rather than reading the mapping readout's account of it.
trajectory.judgement: The printed card shows four separate blocks, which is not evidence about frames, and the readout's story is not evidence about the document's story. What the conversion actually exposes decides whether per-frame mapping exists at all or whether everything runs on offsets inside one story.
trajectory.produces: A true frame inventory and a reconstructed story text.

trajectory.action: Build the mapping against the reconstructed story, validate it, prepare the merge template, then re-export IDML and confirm every expected placeholder is genuinely present in the document.
trajectory.judgement: The validator and the prepare step both report success on mappings that never landed, so the only evidence a field exists in the template is the field itself in the round-tripped document. Choosing to check is the agent's own move.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholders have been confirmed present.

trajectory.action: Merge all twelve records one per page with each casting's own tinted photograph bound through the image column, render for the printer at real output resolution, and look at every card including the two that share a frame.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equals row count on a run where fields are missing, so counting pages proves nothing, and the two castings that share a source frame need a decision rather than a duplicate.
trajectory.produces: A twelve-page press file plus per-record files, and a verdict on every card.

trajectory.action: Create the board and add the finished set, treating a partial success as partial. Then write the note: per frame what was applied, the tone hue, strength and grain, the selection wording that recovered the mark, an honest statement of where the mark holds and where it does not with what to use instead, the type system, anything licensed, and every resize or extension reported.
trajectory.judgement: The note about the mark is the part the foundry will rely on for years, and it has to say plainly what cannot be done with the artwork rather than leave them to find out on a cast plaque or a spec card.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What a mark struck into raw sand-cast iron actually yields as artwork, and whether it survives the two placements the client named. The mark has no ink and no colour of its own: it exists only as the difference between a struck impression and the pitted face around it, and that face carries the same grey inside the letterforms' enclosed counters and inside the border ring as it does outside them. The trace comes back reading convincingly at full canvas, which is the only size anyone would look at it by default, and at the size it reproduces on a spec card the counters have closed solid and the border ring has merged into the letterforms, and reversed on the dark panel ground it loses its remaining edge entirely. Nothing reports any of this. The tracing step takes no options at all, so there is no parameter to have set correctly; the only lever is the raster preparation, and which preparation is needed cannot be chosen until the failure has been seen at real size on the real ground.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it and care cannot pre-empt it. The trace's fidelity is a function of this casting's surface texture, this photograph's light and the selection that produced it. There is no measurement, no preview at delivered size and no parameter on the trace, so an agent that words the selection well and gets the polarity right still cannot know how much of the mark survives without tracing it and putting it on a spec card. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says the mark is struck into the iron and that it has to work small and reversed out of the dark, which is a client naming their hardest placements and their standing requirement exactly as they would to a designer, and asking for a note about where it holds is a request for professional advice rather than a disclosure that the answer is known. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to go back and make a different asset: re-prepare the raster so the impression carries a usable edge before tracing, aim the selection at a different property of the photograph, or accept that the traced mark is a large-format asset and build a different small-size lockup from it, after which the panel, the story page and the cards are re-composed around a mark of a different weight and minimum size.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re-prepare the raster to strengthen the struck edge before tracing rather than trying to repair the trace, re-select on wording aimed at what actually distinguishes the impression in this frame, re-trace, strip the ground path and inject a viewBox again, then re-place at spec-card size and reversed on the dark ground rather than assuming the second attempt took. If it still will not hold small, decide and state what carries that placement instead, and re-author the canvases and the card around the mark's real minimum size.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve spec cards go into the hands of specifiers with the foundry's hundred-year-old maker's mark reproduced as a solid grey blob, and the stand panel carries a mark that has disappeared into its own background, in front of the exact audience the mark exists to reassure.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What last year's card actually becomes as a merge template. Two things are unknowable until the conversion has run and the document has been opened. First, the four cleanly separated blocks on the printed card do not tell you how many text frames the conversion produces, and if they collapse into one continuous story then per-frame mapping does not exist and every field has to be placed by character offset inside a single story, which is a completely different mapping strategy. Second, the mapping readout's account of that story omits one run (the reference line) while keeping the line break that followed it, so the string it reports still looks well formed and every offset after that point is short by that run's length. The validator returns VALID on those wrong offsets with no warnings, and the prepare step reports that the placeholders were created successfully, while some of them silently never landed. Nothing in any tool response distinguishes a template with six live fields from one with four.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. Frame granularity is a property of how the PDF was drawn and is not under the agent's control or knowable from the printed page, and whether the readout's story matches the document's story can only be established by comparing them, which is running the operation. Doing it carefully does not help, because the readout is the artefact that is wrong. (b) Nothing states it. The brief simply says here is last year's print file and the spreadsheet, which is a client handing over what they have. No asset note in the client's hands, no acceptance line and no earlier step names the omitted run or the frame count. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The response is to abandon the mapping strategy and rebuild it on a different basis, offsets computed from the document's own story rather than from the readout, or per-frame replacement if the frames turn out to exist, which is a different mapping rather than the same one re-submitted.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Download and unpack the round-tripped document, reconstruct the story by concatenating its content runs, recompute every offset against that string, rebuild the mapping with the corrected positions in the order the tool requires, prepare the template again and then re-export and search for each placeholder by name rather than trusting the success message. If the frames turned out to be fewer than the printed card suggests, redesign which field goes where before any of that.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Twelve leave-behind cards are printed for a trade fair with the casting reference and the lead time silently absent from every one of them, which is the only information a specifier actually needs in order to call, and every tool in the chain reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether a licensed installation frame can sit with the foundry's own photography under this treatment. Stock search returns a small CDN thumbnail, and the frame's true tonal range, its true black point and how much detail survives in its shadows only exist after it is licensed, downloaded at full resolution and carried under the committed tone. Because everything here maps onto a single hue ramp, colour is not what decides: a candidate joins or fails on luminance structure, and two frames that look equally dark and equally moody at 240 pixels can be a full stop apart once tinted, with one of them turning to a flat black field beside a set built on furnace light and hard speculars. The result is only visible with the licensed frame and the finished set laid out together.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot avoid it. The comparison needs both the licensed frame and the tinted set to exist, so it cannot be moved earlier, and it cannot be settled by care because a thumbnail carries no information about tonal range. (b) Nothing states it. The brief says only that they have no wide installation shot and to buy one if the panel needs it, which is an invitation carrying no claim about how a candidate will behave. (c) It is not a propagation re-run. The likely response is to abandon the frame and search again on different terms, which is a new licensing decision, a new grade and a new judgement, or to resolve it instead by extending one of the foundry's own frames at its edges and accepting a different panel, which changes the panel's composition and the type that sits on it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Push the licensed frame further under the tone, or, if it will not join, return to Stock with a search framed by the tonal structure the set actually has rather than by the subject matter, license a replacement and re-tint it, then lay the whole set out again and judge it as fifteen rather than checking the new frame on its own. If nothing joins, extend one of the foundry's own frames at its edges instead and re-compose the panel around the height that produces.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: The tall panel at a trade fair stand, the largest thing the foundry will put in front of an architect all year, carries a bought photograph that visibly does not belong to the set beside it.

deliverables.name: Ironline Forge editorial image set
deliverables.spec: The shop-floor frames brought from two lighting conditions onto one base and then carried to a single committed dark tone with one hue, one strength and one grain across the set, straightened where the floor line rolled, every output at or below its source dimensions, with per-frame applied settings, every resize, downscale or edge extension any tool reported, and any frame that could not be brought into the set named along with what happened to the placement it was carrying. Delivered at the panel, story and social crops composed for the placement each serves, which are part of this one set rather than separate deliverables.

deliverables.name: Recovered Ironline maker's mark
deliverables.spec: The struck maker's mark recovered from a photograph of a sand-cast bracket as placeable, scalable vector geometry with a real viewBox and no opaque full-canvas ground path, delivered as a transparent mark, an on-dark colourway and a single-colour variant, plus a locally rasterised copy for the handover bundle, together with an honest written statement of where it holds and where it does not, specifically at spec-card reproduction size and reversed on the dark panel ground, and what to use instead wherever it does not. Recovered rather than redrawn: it must still read as the mark in the iron.

deliverables.name: Stand panel, brand story page and social canvas as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: A single native editable Express document carrying the tall stand panel at true physical dimensions, the brand story page and the social canvas, each keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text in one licensed type system, the mark as real vector shapes and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than as a reference. Delivered with the self-contained source it was authored from, because the foundry changes it themselves before the next fair.

deliverables.name: Twelve casting spec cards
deliverables.spec: A live merge template rebuilt from last year's press PDF, since no native file exists, merged against the casting sheet at one record per page: a twelve-page press file in the sheet's order plus per-record files named to the references, each card carrying that casting's own tinted photograph bound through the image column, every mapped field confirmed present in the template itself rather than reported as successful, and every field fully rendered at trim on all twelve, with the two castings that share a source frame resolved rather than duplicated silently.

deliverables.name: Handover note and review board
deliverables.spec: A written note recording the tone hue, strength and grain, per-frame applied settings, the selection wording that recovered the mark, the honest account of the mark's limits and the alternative for the placements it cannot carry, the type system by role with foundry or designer and the actual numeric weight, whether anything was licensed and why, and every resize, downscale or extension any tool reported. Paired with a persistent shareable board carrying the finished set for the client to sign off, with nothing silently dropped.

decision_gates: How dark and how committed the tone goes, given that at this band it has to read as a workshop rather than as a filter.
Whether both lighting conditions are brought onto one base before the tone is committed, or the tone is committed on top of two different bases.
Where a global correction stops working and the move has to be masked to a named material rather than to the object it belongs to, with molten metal and sand wanting opposite moves.
How to word a selection on a mark that has no ink and no colour, where the wording that lifts a printed mark off a substrate has nothing to grip.
Which raster preparation gives the struck impression a usable edge before tracing, given that the tracing step takes no options at all.
Whether the traced mark is a large-format asset only, and if so what carries the spec card and the reversed panel instead.
Which frames can carry the stand panel at its real physical size, and whether to crop tighter, extend at the edges or move the placement when a frame runs short.
What to do about the frames whose floor line rolls, given that the roll is invisible in a full frame and obvious in a tall crop.
Whether the licensed installation frame joins the set under the committed tone, judged on tonal structure rather than colour, and what to do if it does not.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a heritage workshop rather than a supplier catalogue.
Whether the card mapping can be done per frame at all, or whether the conversion forces everything through offsets computed from the document's own story.
How to handle the two castings that share one photograph rather than shipping a visible duplicate.
What to escalate in writing versus what to fix silently, on a commission where the client explicitly asked to be told where their own mark will not work.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a foundry that does not exist and a mark that is not theirs. IDENTITY is the entire commission: the maker's mark is a specific impression cut into a specific die by a specific person's grandfather, struck into every piece the firm sells, and a regenerated version of it is another workshop's mark being passed off as proof of origin to specifiers buying on provenance. The photographs are of this building and these castings, and an architect will stand in front of the panel at the fair. SPEC: the deliverables are defined by numbers and surfaces a generation cannot satisfy, a mark that must be placeable scalable geometry with a real viewBox and no opaque ground path, a stand panel at true physical dimensions produced without inventing a pixel, and twelve cards at one record per page carrying the correct casting's photograph with every mapped field present. EDITABILITY: the panel set exists as a deliverable because the foundry changes it before the next fair, so it has to arrive as a native document with live text and real vector geometry rather than a flat picture of a layout. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: does this trace still read at the size a spec card reproduces it, does this template actually contain the fields the tools said it does, does this licensed frame join the set once both are tinted. None of that is a generation problem, and the honest note about where the mark will not hold is professional advice a render cannot give.
doability_proof: Five surfaces, honestly counted and deliberately not padded: the Illustrator tools are never called because document_render_vector and document_merge_data_vector sit on a polling helper that does not exist in this host, and no video or audio tool is invoked for the same reason. image_vectorize is counted as Photoshop-family, not as an Illustrator surface. Every link is verified in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account). IMAGING: auto_straighten, auto_tone, masked and unmasked image_apply_adjustments, monochromatic_tint and add_grain (both mask-accepting), select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs array, generative_expand and vectorize are all verified headless across the audit's live calls. The extract-and-reuse chain (select, invert, crop to the returned bbox, vectorize, inject a viewBox, delete the opaque first path, inline into HTML, export) is verified end to end on a photographed mark, and the resulting artwork is verified to arrive in Express as real editable vector shapes rather than a flattened image. vectorize takes no options at all, emits no viewBox and always emits an opaque first path, all verified, so the vector hygiene the deliverable gates on is real work the agent must do itself. remove_background is documented as returning a solid opaque disc on a mark inside a ring, which is exactly why the recovery runs through selection, inversion and tracing instead. The prompt-wording asymmetry, where naming the substrate returns the substrate and naming the mark's own visual properties returns the mark, is a verified live finding, and a struck impression in pitted iron is precisely the case where the mark has no colour or medium of its own to name, which is what makes the raster preparation the only lever. Selection masks are verified fully binary with no intermediate values, and crop_and_resize is documented as interpolating to a hard 2x cap and reporting it only in tradeoffs, so the no-invented-pixels bar is scored as a decision plus a disclosure rather than as a measurement. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, true physical canvases resolve exactly at absolute units (mm at 96 dpi), inline SVG becomes native editable vector, external image URLs render as empty grey boxes so every photograph is embedded as image data, and the right-anchored auto-sized wrapper failure and the non-inherited font weight are verified live findings the trajectory designs against. canvasWidth, canvasHeight and slideSelector are never passed as tool params because they are global overrides that collapse a mixed-size set. Transport goes through the text/html upload path because embedded photography passes the inline threshold, and verification is split because the rendition preview shows the first canvas only. Persistence is not assumed, so the deliverable is the editable document plus the self-contained source. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified fully headless and synchronous, a merge template built out of a bare press PDF is verified end to end, one record per page is the confirmed PDF behaviour, real output resolution comes from rendering the merged document rather than from the merge's own ignored resolution field, and per-row image binding through an at-prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles is verified visually. The lossy textContent readout that drops a run while keeping its line break, the validator returning VALID on the resulting wrong offsets, and prepare reporting success while silently dropping mappings are all verified live findings, which is why the trajectory reconstructs the story from the document and re-exports to confirm placeholders. Per-record files come from createSeparateFiles or a recordRange loop because multi-record raster output is documented as returning in reversed order with lying labels. No bleed gate, no named press preset and no variable QR appears anywhere, since all three are documented as unobtainable. FONTS: the recommend, styles, find, kit chain is verified end to end in a real browser, and the non-standard numeric weights, the display-cut-by-slug rule, the slug-not-PostScript CSS rule and the all-or-nothing kit call are live findings the task leans on. STOCK AND BOARDS: short generic queries only because long queries return zero hits, the orientation filter is broken and never passed, licensing returns genuine camera-scale imagery, and boards persist with a twelve-placement cap where 201 means partial success with a failed-items list. VOLUME: eighteen client files in, roughly thirty-four artefacts moved in total, every multi-image call at or under the ten-item cap and no batch above twenty. AVOIDED: no text-to-image, no generative fill, no AI object removal, no background-replace-by-prompt, no upscaling, no OCR, no compositing, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no replace_image, no download_design, and no photograph or mark reaching Express as a URL.
